Bialystok Old Jewish Cemetery (Rabbinic)

Jewish Cemetery · Białystok, Poland

Demolished. The plot for this, Białystok's second Jewish cemetery, was bought by the Jewish community in 1752. During the 1920 Polish-Soviet War, about 50 people were buried here; burials continued even during the Białystok Ghetto period of WWII. The cemetery was officially closed around 1890 as part of a general plan to relocate cemeteries beyond city limits. After the war, tombstones were stolen and graves robbed, and debris from the bombed city's cleanup was dumped on the site; from 1950, construction projects took over parts of the land, with the remainder becoming today's Park Centralny.
